Derives from survival needs that become apparent when people recognize that failure to accept those who are different and treat them justly will lead to strife, and when people become aware of the scarcity of natural resources.", "core_value": "universalism", "sources": [{"entry_id": "5fa8b540:entry:2", "journal_entry": "Interesting thing happened during morning assembly. One of my Class 3 students, Ravi, came up to me after and said he told his mother about the water pollution lesson I did last week. She apparently asked him to explain it again because their neighborhood has been complaining about the nala running brown. He was so proud of himself, like he'd done something important.

And maybe he did? A nine-year-old going home and talking to his family about why their water is dirty—that feels like something actually working. Not in a big dramatic way, just a small thread pulling in the right direction. I changed nothing about anyone's pipes but now one family is paying attention. That's enough for today.", "nudge_response": null}, {"entry_id": "5fa8b540:entry:1", "journal_entry": "Went to the literacy camp in Sultanpur today and I keep thinking about this one girl, maybe seven or eight, who was holding the pencil like she'd never held one before. And honestly she probably hadn't. She was gripping it so tight her knuckles were white and she kept looking at me like she was asking permission to write her own name.

I sat with her for almost an hour. The other volunteers were doing group activities but I just couldn't move on from this kid. Her name is Fatima. She got the first two letters right and then she looked at me and smiled and it was like, okay, this is why I wake up early on Saturdays and take that awful bus that takes ninety minutes one way.

I know this sounds naive or whatever. Didi would say I'm romanticizing things. But I was there today and she wasn't. There's something about being in the room with someone who just learned they can write their own name that makes all the other noise—the salary complaints, Baba asking when I'll "move up," the crumbling school building—feel small.
